# heed

**Embeddable, no-install, framework-agnostic end-user feedback** — a drop-in widget
that lets *any visitor* of your deployed web app report a bug or request a feature,
with useful context gathered automatically, routed to a pluggable backend (GitHub
Issues first). Works standalone; integrates cleanly with
[`enlace`](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace) as an optional add-on, but does **not**
depend on it.

> **Status: design phase.** The competitive landscape, the design rationale, and the
> roadmap live in [`misc/docs/`](). Work is tracked in GitHub
> [issues](https://github.com/i2mint/heed/issues); design decisions in GitHub
> [discussions](https://github.com/i2mint/heed/discussions).

## Why

Developer-side tools (browser extensions, Chrome DevTools MCP, Jam, …) only help
*you*. They can never serve an ordinary end user reporting a problem on your live
site, or asking for a feature. `heed` is the missing piece: a **public, zero-install**
capture-and-report widget plus a small self-hostable backend that *you* own and that
routes wherever you want.

## The shape (planned)

- **Widget** — one `<script>` tag injects a Shadow-DOM-isolated custom element; drops
  into React, plain HTML, or server-rendered pages alike. Captures a screenshot, page
  URL, and environment by default; console/network capture is *opt-in* (privacy).
- **Backend** — a mountable FastAPI router (run on its own, or mounted into `enlace`)
  that validates, stores attachments (via `dol`), and dispatches to a **pluggable
  sink**.
- **Sinks** (strategy pattern) — GitHub Issues / Discussions first; email, Slack, a
  built-in board, or a database later.
- **Agent hand-off** — an optional MCP server (`py2mcp`) so Claude Code can pull the
  feedback queue and act on reports.

## Design principles

- **Standalone first.** No hard `enlace` dependency; enlace integration is an optional
  `[enlace]` extra with lazy imports.
- **Privacy by default.** Heavy capture (console, network, session replay) is opt-in;
  PII masking is designed in, not bolted on.
- **Public endpoint = hostile input.** Rate limiting, origin checks, payload caps, and
  bot protection are first-class — the ingest endpoint is unauthenticated by nature.
- **Progressive disclosure.** One script tag works out of the box; everything is
  parametrizable via keyword-only options with smart defaults.

## Install

```bash
pip install heed                 # core (backend + models)
pip install "heed[github]"       # + GitHub sink
pip install "heed[enlace,mcp]"   # + enlace mount + MCP feedback queue
pip install "heed[redis]"        # + rate limits shared across workers
```

## Running the ingest endpoint safely

The `POST /report` endpoint is public, so it ships hardened: origin allow-list with CORS, streamed body/field/screenshot caps, strict input validation, per-IP and per-origin rate limits, a honeypot field, and an optional Turnstile/hCaptcha gate. Configure it in code or from `HEED_*` environment variables:

```python
from heed import HeedConfig, StoreSink, make_app

config = HeedConfig.from_env()   # e.g. HEED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://myapp.example
app = make_app(StoreSink({}), config=config)
```

For production, set `allowed_origins`, `trusted_proxies` (behind a reverse proxy), `rate_limit_backend="redis"` with `redis_url` (several workers), and `bot_secret` to turn the bot gate on. Embedders also need a Content-Security-Policy that allows the widget: see [`misc/docs/embedding-security.md`]().

## Documents

- [`misc/docs/research-report.md`]() — the competitive
  landscape: what to reuse / steal / avoid, design patterns, and gotchas (deep
  research with adversarial verification).
- [`misc/docs/design.md`]() — architecture, the data model, the
  sink interface, and the spectrum of approaches with pros/cons.
- [`misc/docs/embedding-security.md`]() — hardening knobs for operators and CSP guidance for sites that embed the widget.

# _autosummary/heed.base.html.md

# heed.base

Domain model for heed — the single source of truth shared by widget and backend.

Everything that crosses the widget↔backend boundary, or moves between the ingest
layer and a sink, is one of the Pydantic models defined here. The widget POSTs a
[`ReportSubmission`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.ReportSubmission) (what an untrusted client may assert); the backend enriches
it into a [`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report) (server-assigned id, timestamp, resolved identity, validated
origin, status) before handing it to a sink.

### Functions

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`utcnow`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.utcnow)()                  | Return the current UTC time (an injectable clock seam for tests).       |

# _autosummary/heed.config.html.md

# heed.config

Configuration for the heed backend (smart defaults; keyword-only).

Every knob has a safe default, so `HeedConfig()` works out of the box for a
single-worker deployment. [`HeedConfig.from_env()`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig.from_env) reads the same knobs from
`HEED_*` environment variables, which is where secrets (the bot-gate key) and
infrastructure (the Redis URL) belong.

### Classes

| [`HeedConfig`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig)(\*[, allowed_origins, ...])   | Knobs for the ingest endpoint.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|

### *class* heed.config.HeedConfig(\*, allowed_origins=None, handle_cors=True, cors_allow_credentials=False, cors_max_age_seconds=600, max_body_bytes=6000000, max_screenshot_bytes=5000000, max_field_bytes=100000, max_form_fields=16, rate_limit_per_minute=30, origin_rate_limit_per_minute=600, rate_limit_window_seconds=60.0, rate_limit_backend='memory', redis_url=None, trusted_proxies=<factory>, ipv6_rate_limit_prefix=64, bot_gate=None, bot_secret=None, bot_expected_hostnames=None, bot_token_field='bot_token', honeypot_field='hp_website', accept_console=False, accept_network=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Knobs for the ingest endpoint. All optional with sensible defaults.

#### *property* bot_gate_enabled *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

True when a bot-gate secret is configured.

#### *classmethod* from_env(environ=None, \*\*overrides)

Build a config from `HEED_<FIELD>` variables, then apply `overrides`.

Lists are comma-separated; booleans accept 1/true/yes/on; `none` unsets an
optional knob (e.g. `HEED_ORIGIN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=none`).

* **Return type:**
  [`HeedConfig`](_autosummary/heed.config.html.md#heed.config.HeedConfig)

```pycon
>>> cfg = HeedConfig.from_env(
...     {"HEED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "https://a.example, https://b.example",
...      "HEED_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE": "10"}
... )
>>> cfg.allowed_origins, cfg.rate_limit_per_minute
(['https://a.example', 'https://b.example'], 10)
```


# _autosummary/heed.html.md

# heed

heed — embeddable, no-install, framework-agnostic end-user feedback.

`heed` lets any visitor of a deployed web app report a bug or request a feature, with
useful context gathered automatically, routed to a pluggable backend (GitHub Issues
first). It works standalone and integrates with `enlace` as an optional add-on,
without depending on it.

Phase 1 ships the backend core (the widget is tracked in issue #6). The competitive
landscape and design rationale live in `misc/docs/`.

Public API (Phase 1):
: Models    Report, ReportSubmission, Identity, Environment, Category, Status,
  : Attachment, LogEntry, NetEntry
  <br/>
  Sinks     Sink, BaseSink, SinkResult, StoreSink, GitHubIssuesSink,
  : github_sink_from_token
  <br/>
  Backend   process_submission, make_router, make_app, HeedConfig
  Hardening RateLimiter, InMemoryRateLimiter, RedisRateLimiter, make_rate_limiter,
  <br/>
  > BotVerifier, SiteverifyBotVerifier, make_bot_verifier
  > (see misc/docs/embedding-security.md)
  <br/>
  Storage   make_report_store, make_attachment_store

### Example

```pycon
>>> from heed import StoreSink, ReportSubmission, process_submission
>>> store = {}
>>> report, result = process_submission(
...     ReportSubmission(title="Login button does nothing"), StoreSink(store)
... )
>>> result.ok and report.id in store
True
```

### Functions

| [`new_report_id`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.new_report_id)()                                   | Return a fresh opaque report id (uuid4 hex).                                  |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`github_sink_from_token`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.github_sink_from_token)(repo, token, \*\*kwargs)   | Build a GitHubIssuesSink that creates issues in `repo` ('owner/name').        |
| [`process_submission`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.process_submission)(submission, sink, \*[, ...])   | Enrich `submission` into a Report, store any screenshot, and route to `sink`. |
| [`make_router`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_router)(sink, \*[, config, ...])              | Build a FastAPI APIRouter exposing `POST /report` (and its CORS preflight).   |
| [`make_app`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_app)(sink, \*[, config, ...])                 | A standalone FastAPI app serving the heed router under `prefix`.              |
| [`make_rate_limiter`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_rate_limiter)([backend, window_seconds, ...]) | Build a limiter from the `rate_limiter_backends` registry by name.            |
| [`make_bot_verifier`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_bot_verifier)(provider, secret, \*\*kwargs)   | Return a verifier, or `None` (gate off) when no secret is configured.         |
| [`make_report_store`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_report_store)([rootdir])                      | A text store for report JSON.                                                 |
| [`make_attachment_store`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.make_attachment_store)([rootdir])                  | A bytes store for attachments.                                                |

### *class* heed.InMemoryRateLimiter(\*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, max_keys=100000, clock=<built-in function monotonic>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Sliding-window, in-memory limiter. Per process — NOT shared across workers.

Fine for a single-worker deployment; with several workers each one counts alone,
so the effective limit is multiplied. Use [`RedisRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.html.md#heed.RedisRateLimiter) there. The
number of tracked keys is bounded (`max_keys`, least-recently-seen evicted) so a
flood of distinct keys cannot exhaust memory.

### *class* heed.RedisRateLimiter(client, \*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, namespace='heed:rl', fallback=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Fixed-window limiter in Redis — one count shared by every worker and host.

`client` is any redis-py compatible client (injected; tests use a fake). When
Redis errors, the request is decided by `fallback` (a per-process in-memory
limiter by default), so an outage degrades protection instead of either dropping
all feedback or removing the limit.

#### *classmethod* from_url(url, , socket_timeout=0.5, \*\*kwargs)

Build from a `redis://` URL (needs the `[redis]` extra).

`socket_timeout` bounds both connect and reads, so a hung Redis costs at most
that long before the fallback limiter decides.

* **Return type:**

# _autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md

# heed.ingest

The ingest layer — build a Report from a submission and route it to a sink.

`process_submission` is the pure, framework-free core (dependency-injected sink,
stores, clock, id generator) so it is unit-testable without a server. `make_router`
wraps it in a FastAPI `APIRouter` you can run standalone (`make_app`) or
`include_router` into an enlace app. Identity is anonymous by default; pass a
`user_dependency` to bind identity when an auth layer (e.g. enlace_auth) is present.

The router treats every request as hostile (see `security.py` and issue #5). Checks
run cheapest-first so abuse is rejected before it costs anything: CORS preflight →
origin allow-list → per-IP rate limit (both before `user_dependency`) → body-size cap
(streamed, before parsing) → form limits → honeypot → bot gate → per-origin rate limit
→ model validation → screenshot sniffing.

#### NOTE
this module does not `from __future__ import annotations` — FastAPI resolves
route-handler annotations against module globals, so the request/response types are
imported at module level.

### Functions

| [`make_app`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.make_app)(sink, \*[, config, ...])               | A standalone FastAPI app serving the heed router under `prefix`.              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_router`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.make_router)(sink, \*[, config, ...])            | Build a FastAPI APIRouter exposing `POST /report` (and its CORS preflight).   |
| [`process_submission`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.process_submission)(submission, sink, \*[, ...]) | Enrich `submission` into a Report, store any screenshot, and route to `sink`. |
| [`read_capped_body`](_autosummary/heed.ingest.html.md#heed.ingest.read_capped_body)(request, \*, max_bytes)        | Read the request body, or return None as soon as it exceeds `max_bytes`.      |

Build a FastAPI APIRouter exposing `POST /report` (and its CORS preflight).

Hardening defaults come from `config`; any piece can be injected instead:

  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Report`](_autosummary/heed.base.html.md#heed.base.Report), [`SinkResult`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.SinkResult)]

# _autosummary/heed.security.html.md

# heed.security

Public-endpoint hardening (the ingest endpoint is unauthenticated and hostile).

Everything here is a small function or a strategy behind a protocol, so the router
composes them and deployments swap implementations without touching it:

- **Origins / CORS**: [`origin_allowed()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.origin_allowed), [`cors_headers()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.cors_headers),
  [`preflight_headers()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.preflight_headers).
- **Client identity for rate limiting**: [`client_ip()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.client_ip) (honours
  `X-Forwarded-For` only from trusted proxies).
- **Rate limiting**: the [`RateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RateLimiter) protocol, an in-memory default
  ([`InMemoryRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.InMemoryRateLimiter), per process) and [`RedisRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RedisRateLimiter) (shared
  across workers), looked up by name via [`make_rate_limiter()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.make_rate_limiter).
- **Bot gate**: the [`BotVerifier`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.BotVerifier) protocol and [`SiteverifyBotVerifier`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.SiteverifyBotVerifier)
  for Cloudflare Turnstile / hCaptcha, built by [`make_bot_verifier()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.make_bot_verifier) only when a
  secret is configured (off otherwise).
- **Attachments**: [`sniff_image_type()`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.sniff_image_type) checks screenshot magic bytes.

### Functions

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`make_rate_limiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.make_rate_limiter)([backend, window_seconds, ...]) | Build a limiter from the `rate_limiter_backends` registry by name.              |
| [`normalize_origin`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.normalize_origin)(origin)                          | Canonical form of an origin for comparison (lower-case, no trailing slash).     |
| [`origin_allowed`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.origin_allowed)(origin, allowed)                   | True if origin is permitted; `allowed=None` allows any (the dev default).       |
| [`parse_networks`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.parse_networks)(proxies)                           | Parse IPs/CIDRs (strings or network objects) into networks; raises ValueError.  |
| [`preflight_headers`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.preflight_headers)(origin, allowed, \*[, ...])     | Headers answering a CORS preflight, or `{}` when the origin is not allowed.     |
| [`rate_limit_key`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.rate_limit_key)(ip, \*[, ipv6_prefix])             | The bucket key for `ip`: IPv4 as-is, IPv6 grouped by its /`ipv6_prefix`.        |
| [`sniff_image_type`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.sniff_image_type)(data)                            | The media type of `data` from its magic bytes, or None if not an allowed image. |

### *class* heed.security.BotVerifier(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Verify a human-challenge token server-side; True means “looks human”.

### *class* heed.security.InMemoryRateLimiter(\*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, max_keys=100000, clock=<built-in function monotonic>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Sliding-window, in-memory limiter. Per process — NOT shared across workers.

Fine for a single-worker deployment; with several workers each one counts alone,
so the effective limit is multiplied. Use [`RedisRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RedisRateLimiter) there. The
number of tracked keys is bounded (`max_keys`, least-recently-seen evicted) so a
flood of distinct keys cannot exhaust memory.

### *class* heed.security.RateLimiter(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Decide whether a request keyed by `key` (e.g. client IP) is allowed now.

### *class* heed.security.RedisRateLimiter(client, \*, max_per_window=30, window_seconds=60.0, namespace='heed:rl', fallback=None, clock=<built-in function time>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Fixed-window limiter in Redis — one count shared by every worker and host.

`client` is any redis-py compatible client (injected; tests use a fake). When
Redis errors, the request is decided by `fallback` (a per-process in-memory
limiter by default), so an outage degrades protection instead of either dropping
all feedback or removing the limit.

#### *classmethod* from_url(url, , socket_timeout=0.5, \*\*kwargs)

Build from a `redis://` URL (needs the `[redis]` extra).

`socket_timeout` bounds both connect and reads, so a hung Redis costs at most
that long before the fallback limiter decides.

* **Return type:**
  [`RedisRateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RedisRateLimiter)

### *class* heed.security.SiteverifyBotVerifier(secret, \*, verify_url='https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify', expected_hostnames=None, timeout=5.0, max_token_chars=4096, http_post=<function \_urllib_post_form>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Turnstile / hCaptcha verification (both speak the same siteverify protocol).

Fails closed: a missing token, a network error, or a malformed answer all verify
as False. `expected_hostnames`, when given, also rejects tokens solved on
another site. `http_post` is injectable (tests never touch the network).

### heed.security.client_ip(peer, forwarded_for, , trusted_proxies=())

The client address to rate-limit on.

`X-Forwarded-For` is attacker-controlled unless the direct peer is a trusted
proxy, so it is only consulted then — and read right-to-left, skipping trusted
hops, so a client cannot prepend a fake address.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> client_ip("10.0.0.1", "6.6.6.6, 1.2.3.4", trusted_proxies=["10.0.0.0/8"])
'1.2.3.4'
>>> client_ip("5.5.5.5", "1.2.3.4")  # untrusted peer: header ignored
'5.5.5.5'
```

### heed.security.cors_headers(origin, allowed, , allow_credentials=False)

CORS response headers for `origin`, or `{}` when it is not allowed.

The request’s own origin is echoed (never `*`) so the response is correct with
or without credentials; `Vary: Origin` keeps shared caches honest.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### heed.security.make_bot_verifier(provider, secret, \*\*kwargs)

Return a verifier, or `None` (gate off) when no secret is configured.

`provider` defaults to `"turnstile"` when a secret is given.

* **Return type:**
  [`BotVerifier`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.BotVerifier) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### heed.security.make_rate_limiter(backend='memory', , max_per_window, window_seconds=60.0, namespace='ip', redis_url=None)

Build a limiter from the `rate_limiter_backends` registry by name.

* **Return type:**
  [`RateLimiter`](_autosummary/heed.security.html.md#heed.security.RateLimiter)

### heed.security.normalize_origin(origin)

Canonical form of an origin for comparison (lower-case, no trailing slash).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> normalize_origin("HTTPS://App.Example/")
'https://app.example'
```

### heed.security.origin_allowed(origin, allowed)

True if origin is permitted; `allowed=None` allows any (the dev default).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

```pycon
>>> origin_allowed("https://a.example", ["https://a.example"])
True
>>> origin_allowed(None, ["https://a.example"])
False
```

### heed.security.parse_networks(proxies)

Parse IPs/CIDRs (strings or network objects) into networks; raises ValueError.

Call it once at startup so a typo fails loudly there, not on every request.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`IPv4Network`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/ipaddress.html#ipaddress.IPv4Network) | [`IPv6Network`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/ipaddress.html#ipaddress.IPv6Network)]

```pycon
>>> parse_networks(["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.0/8"])
[IPv4Network('127.0.0.1/32'), IPv4Network('10.0.0.0/8')]
```

### heed.security.preflight_headers(origin, allowed, , allow_credentials=False, max_age_seconds=600, methods='POST, OPTIONS', request_headers=None)

Headers answering a CORS preflight, or `{}` when the origin is not allowed.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### heed.security.rate_limit_key(ip, , ipv6_prefix=64)

The bucket key for `ip`: IPv4 as-is, IPv6 grouped by its /`ipv6_prefix`.

One IPv6 host typically owns a whole /64, so per-address buckets are trivially
dodged by rotating addresses.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> rate_limit_key("2001:db8::1") == rate_limit_key("2001:db8::ffff")
True
>>> rate_limit_key("1.2.3.4")
'1.2.3.4'
```

### heed.security.sniff_image_type(data)

The media type of `data` from its magic bytes, or None if not an allowed image.

Never trust the client’s declared content type: an “image” might be HTML/SVG.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

```pycon
>>> sniff_image_type(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n...")
'image/png'
>>> sniff_image_type(b"<svg onload=alert(1)>") is None
True
```


# _autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md

# heed.sinks.base

The sink abstraction — where a report goes (strategy pattern).

A sink is the only thing that decides what becomes of a report. The ingest layer calls
`Sink.submit()`; richer sinks may also offer duplicate detection and
acknowledgement. New destinations are added by writing a sink, never by editing a
dispatcher.

| [`Sink`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.Sink)(\*args, \*\*kwargs) | Anything that can receive a report.                                     |
| [`SinkResult`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.base.html.md#heed.sinks.base.SinkResult)(\*\*data)     | Outcome of routing a report to a sink.                                  |

### *class* heed.sinks.base.BaseSink

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Convenience base giving no-op defaults for the optional sink methods.

  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

# _autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md

# heed.sinks.github

A sink that turns a report into a GitHub issue.

The issue-creating call is dependency-injected (`create_issue`) so the sink is
testable without network access and so the credential-brokering strategy (a GitHub App
minting short-lived installation tokens, or a server-side token) is pluggable. A
convenience factory builds a `create_issue` from a token via `ghapi` (lazy import,
the `heed[github]` extra).

Hard platform limit (see misc/docs/design.md): there is no GitHub API to attach an image
to an issue. Resolve a `screenshot_url` (committed-file / attachment-store URL) and
embed it in the body; base64 data-URIs do not render.

### Functions

| [`github_sink_from_token`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.github_sink_from_token)(repo, token, \*\*kwargs)   | Build a GitHubIssuesSink that creates issues in `repo` ('owner/name').   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`render_issue_body`](_autosummary/heed.sinks.github.html.md#heed.sinks.github.render_issue_body)(report, \*[, screenshot_url])   | Render a report as a GitHub-flavoured markdown issue body.               |

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/heed.storage.html.md

# heed.storage

Storage helpers — dol-backed stores for reports and binary attachments.

Stores are plain `MutableMapping``s, so the rest of heed never depends on a specific
backend. Defaults are in-memory; pass a directory to persist to the filesystem, or
inject any ``dol` store (S3, Mongo, …).

### Functions

| [`make_attachment_store`](_autosummary/heed.storage.html.md#heed.storage.make_attachment_store)([rootdir])   | A bytes store for attachments.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| [`make_report_store`](_autosummary/heed.storage.html.md#heed.storage.make_report_store)([rootdir])       | A text store for report JSON.    |

### heed.storage.make_attachment_store(rootdir=None)

A bytes store for attachments. In-memory unless `rootdir` is given.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### heed.storage.make_report_store(rootdir=None)

A text store for report JSON. In-memory unless `rootdir` is given.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

# For AI agents

`heed` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/i2mint/heed/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://i2mint.github.io/heed/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`heed.md`](https://i2mint.github.io/heed/heed.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://i2mint.github.io/heed/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
